approach: The scale reads correctly within the temperature range where the length error caused by expansion or contraction stays within the stated 0.5 mm tolerance.

steps.text: Write the length of the metre scale and the allowed error.
Find the temperature change that produces exactly this length error.
The scale can be used this many degrees above or below the temperature it was made at.
steps.why_this_step: Below the making temperature the metal contracts, making marked lengths too long; above it, the metal expands, making them too short; both directions are limited by the same 0.5 mm tolerance.

common_mistakes.text: Extending the temperature range only above 25°C, from 25°C to 75°C, misses that the scale also misreads by the same amount when cooled below the making temperature.
Treating the 0.5 mm tolerance as split evenly into ±0.25 mm instead of the full 0.5 mm allowed each way gives a narrower range of 0°C to +50°C.
